title: CR 2026-08-23-001 (waveform progress + BPM detection) — Howler capability assessment, expanded design, world-review incorporation
outcome: Expanded the UI-enhancements change request in place (original text preserved verbatim) after a capability assessment: Howler 2.2.3 provides NEITHER a waveform/peak API NOR metadata/BPM analysis, and the decoded buffer is not retrievable from a Howl (research §5 pitfall 5) — but Metronomad already decodes and owns the AudioBuffer itself (fileLoader.js → _buffer), so both features build on standard Web Audio AudioBuffer accessors with zero new dependencies and zero Howler involvement (its role per howlerSetup.js is unchanged). The expansion adds, per feature: data/pipeline design (peak extraction with 4096-bucket high-res cache + min/max pooling; pure-DSP tempo detection = mono mixdown → leading-silence trim → half-wave-rectified frame-energy onset envelope → autocorrelation over 30–250 BPM with a 70–180 prior + confidence threshold), rendering/interaction/a11y design (canvas + div overlays; playhead re-uses the existing progressPercent computed on the 10 Hz songPosition tick — no second RAF loop, honoring D9; canvas role=slider for the offset with full keyboard parity table, .progress-readout role=progressbar for progress), state/memory (non-reactive handles, generation guards), draft acceptance criteria, test/E2E hook plans (KB-6 convention), open questions, and out-of-scope/limitations. Then ran the world-review subagent (qwen-agentworld-35b-a3b) over the expansion: 17 findings (W-1…W-17) — all incorporated in place with W-number citations and a full disposition table in §6; the most consequential were: sampleRate is not a constant (44.1/48/96 kHz depending on browser/device — both pure modules take it as an explicit input), the dual slider+progressbar role split, pointercancel + try/catch pointer-capture + touch-action: pan-y, confidence-metric/'null when unsure' contract for BPM (wrong-but-confident is worse than no suggestion), and generation guards for file-replaced/unmount mid-flight async tasks. Two reviewer suggestions were explicitly rejected with reasoning (keeping the native range alongside the canvas; requestIdleCallback as v1 default). Token/duration figures measured from the session JSONL (main agent only; the world-review subagent's own usage is in a separate session).
key_decisions: Expanded the CR in place (original requests preserved verbatim at top) rather than a companion document — the CR file is the planning artifact and a single source is easier for the planner to consume

Answer to the user's Howler question: no, Howler provides neither feature — but the question is moot because the app owns the decoded AudioBuffer itself (Option B architecture); the CR states this as a capability assessment with evidence pointers (research §4/§5, fileLoader.js, howlerSetup.js) rather than a bare yes/no

O-1 disposition: the waveform canvas REPLACES #offsetScrubber (world-review's coexistence suggestion rejected as a redundant control), with parity restored deliberately — full keyboard table (←/→ 0.1 s, Shift 1 s, PageUp/Down 10 % of duration, Home/End), aria-* wiring, and a manual VoiceOver/NVDA acceptance pass

ARIA split (W-10): one element, one role — canvas = slider (offset only), .progress-readout = progressbar (song position; identical values/semantics the current .progress div carries, role simply moved to the visible-value element; not a live region, so 10 Hz value changes are query-only, no SR churn)

Playhead design: no per-frame imperative code and no second clock — it binds to the existing progressPercent computed (songPosition is already 10 Hz-throttled by createBeatDots per D9); under prefers-reduced-motion the playhead STAYS (functional position indicator, like a video scrubber's) with no CSS animation added — disposition recorded so it is not 'fixed' away later

BPM detection: pure energy-envelope + autocorrelation DSP (no FFT, no new dependency); container-metadata path (ID3/Vorbis) deferred with written rationale (no standard BPM frame in mp3/m4a; Vorbis BPM= occasional; ~100-line parser for a low hit-rate); musical prior 70–180 BPM + explicit confidence metric with conservative threshold and the product principle 'no suggestion > wrong suggestion'; half-time pairs inside the prior band (75/150) documented as an accepted ambiguity pinned by test

BPM prefill is suggestion-only, gated by three structural conditions (confidence threshold, bpmTouchedThisFile flag with an explicit lifecycle table, field unfocused + draft==model) — auto-prefill deliberately does NOT set the touched flag, so a re-drop re-suggests and the user can still correct the suggestion

Both async post-load tasks (peaks, tempo) carry the D4 generation/buffer-identity guard (file-replaced mid-flight and unmount mid-flight both drop the stale result) — the engine's generation-counter discipline extended to UI-side async work

World-review addendum recorded as a W-1…W-17 disposition table (§6) with findings incorporated in place (each CR section cites its W-numbers) and rejections justified inline — the reviewer's output is auditable without re-running the subagent
learnings: 'Can library X do feature Y?' questions for Metronomad should first be answered with 'does the app already own the data Y needs?' — the Option B architecture (app decodes its own AudioBuffer) makes Howler's missing analysis APIs irrelevant; the same reasoning will apply to any future feature touching decoded audio (offset-to-beat snap, loop points)

AudioBuffer.sampleRate is NOT a constant: Chromium/Firefox resample decoded buffers to the AudioContext (device) rate (commonly 48 kHz) while some WebKit builds return the file's native rate — any pure DSP function must take sampleRate as an explicit parameter, and tests must cover at least two rates or the math is only pinned at 44.1 kHz by accident (world-review W-8 caught this in the CR's illustrative '44.1 kHz' figures)

ARIA: never load one element with both an interactive role (slider) and a read-only role (progressbar) — split by role and attach each to the element whose visible meaning it carries; a progressbar that is not a live region sidesteps 10 Hz announcement churn entirely (world-review W-10)

The D4 generation guard is not engine-specific — ANY UI-side async task started after a state change (peak extraction, tempo detection) can be raced by a newer file landing mid-flight or by unmount (N-14 precedent); the guard is a buffer-identity/epoch check after every await-yield, not a flag on the task

Emitting a ~21 KB document in a single write tool call can hit the response output-token limit and silently truncate the arguments — split large doc writes into a first chunk ending in a marker comment + an edit that replaces the marker with the remainder

World-review (qwen-agentworld-35b-a3b) proved strong at design-stage review when the prompt names the exact CR sections, the concrete code paths to ground in, and the specific edge-case families to probe (sample rates, pointer capture on iOS, half-time music, stale async) — its generic findings were few when the prompt was that specific; the single most valuable correction (sampleRate) came from probing 'do the 44.1 kHz assumptions hold on 48 kHz files?'
next_steps: USER: review the expanded CR — decisions most worth a look: O-1 (waveform replaces the range scrubber), the BPM prefill contract + flag table (§2.5), the reduced-motion playhead disposition (§1.4), and the §6 W-table dispositions/rejections

PLANNER: when the user green-lights, decompose the CR into _agent_docs/plans/ (candidate phases: (1) shared onBufferLoaded hook + waveform view, (2) tempo detection + prefill UX); plan-time pins still owed: exact hint/announcement strings, the confidence-metric formula + threshold, responsive waveform breakpoints/heights, PageUp/Down step choice, and the new 120 BPM click-train E2E fixture generation

build-tdd: new suites will be MyComponents/WaveformPeaksTest.html and MyComponents/TempoDetectionTest.html (synthetic data only — no real AudioContext per engine-test convention, except possibly one buffer-render case); E2E needs the known-tempo fixture and the in-page timing assertions per the existing conventions
No commit needed — _agent_docs/ is gitignored (repo learning 2026-08-22); commit responsibility is build-quick-work's anyway
